claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26 the Infrastructure Committee rejected administration's recommended hold on the remaining routes (R, Recommendation 1 of IS03688) rather than adopting it, and City Council had not adopted the hold by 2026-09-25. First I checked whether R proposed a hold under claim 2's primary deferral definition, reading the report as a whole with the operative Attachment 5.
claims.interpretation_notes: ORDER OF CLASSIFICATION: No body adopted R by 2026-09-25, so Contradicted does not apply. The operative version can be read (Version 2 is the declared primary; see claim 2), so the hold/no-hold ladder applies. HOLD DETERMINATION: Under Version 2 (DocumentId 304030), R did NOT propose a hold on my reading. V2 says the remaining routes 'will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications' and that 'In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report ... for Council direction and approval'. It never says those routes wait for that report. Treating them as held needs an inference from the contrast with 'will continue as planned'. The report body's 'construction is best postponed to 2027' covers all unstarted routes, including routes continuing as planned, and it is tied to weather, not to an evaluation. Under the original (304032) and Version 1 (304031), R DID propose a hold: 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed'. COMMITTEE DISPOSITION: The item 7.6 minutes record no motion to adopt R, moved or put. The only substantive motion was A. Salvador's to 'Continue implementation ... in accordance with the previously approved scope of Capital Profile CM-20-0330' and to advance tender-ready routes. That motion is incompatible with R, and it was Defeated 2 to 2. An amendment by E. Rutherford was also Defeated 2 to 2. The only motion carried on the item kept Attachment 4 private (4 to 0). This is 'leaving R without a decision': no motion adopting R was moved, and no incompatible motion carried. It is not 'rejecting R'. CLASSIFICATION: No hold (V2, primary): Partially supported. What is established is that the recommendation was not adopted. What is not established is that what was declined was a hold. Hold (original/V1): committee left R without a decision, so Partially supported again. Here it is not established that members voted R down or voted to proceed against it; the pro-continuation motion failed. The verdict is therefore the same under every version. ALTERNATIVE 'did not support' reading (non-adoption suffices): Supported. ALTERNATIVE BODY (City Council as a body of 13): the carried Council minutes for 2026-09-08/16 show no item on R or IS03688 except a notice of motion, so R had not come before Council by the as-of date. Result: Not established for Council as a body. OVERRIDE STRAND: The committee made no decision on R. Its only item 7.6 decision was to keep Attachment 4 private. No later Council decision is incompatible with it, so the minutes show no override. The absence of a later Council item is an absence, not an override and not agreement. MEMBERSHIP: Committee members present were E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Paquette, and Mayor A. Knack (a member under s.15(3), Bylaw 18156). Paquette was absent with notice for part of the meeting. Knack and Paquette are not recorded on the amendment, the main motion, or the Attachment 4 motion; the open data voting record marks both 'absent' on those votes. Councillors Elliott, Morgan, Parmar, Principe, Stevenson, Tang and Wright attended but were not committee members. WHAT GOVERNED AFTERWARDS: The previously approved CM-20-0330 ($100,000,000 approved 2022, City Council Budget, CBA 7, carried 9-4) and the 2026-07-07 Council motion changing the 50 Street design (carried 9-3). There was no Council decision on R. Administration's statements are reported separately: report IS03688 says 'for routes where construction has not yet started, construction is best postponed to 2027'. Attachment 3 says six routes' 'installation in 2026 is no longer viable' and 'Next steps for these segments will depend on Council's direction'.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In report IS03688 for the Infrastructure Committee of 2026-08-26, City administration recommended an approach that expressly defers construction or advancement of 14 named, unbuilt routes of the programme until a further evaluation, report or decision. Operative version: Version 2 (DocumentId 304030), as the brief declares, because the minutes list both replacements without distinguishing them.
claims.interpretation_notes: OPERATIVE VERSION: The item 1.4 minutes adopted the agenda with 'Replacement attachments ... 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)'. Item 7.6 lists all three versions. Nothing identifies which one the committee considered, so the operative version is uncertain and Version 2 is the primary reading. RECOMMENDATION 1 asks for approval of 'the updated approach ... as outlined in Attachment 5' ('Council decision required'), addressed to Infrastructure Committee to recommend to City Council. VERSION 2 (304030): Primary deferral reading NOT met. V2 says routes without impacts 'will continue as planned' and 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications'. It adds 'In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report outlining trade-offs and options for the remaining routes ... for Council direction and approval' and 'If Council approves the approach, the following projects may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' That is re-evaluation plus a report back. No passage in V2, in the report body, or in Attachment 3 says the listed routes wait for that report. The report's 'construction is best postponed to 2027' covers every unstarted route, including routes continuing as planned, and it is tied to weather. Attachment 3's 'Next steps for these segments will depend on Council's direction' refers to this report, not to a further evaluation. This is the pivotal judgment, and I rate it a close call. The stricter reading (removed, or will not proceed) is also NOT met. ORIGINAL (304032): primary met ('would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed'; the listed projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027' and 'may be revisited' after Administration evaluates legislative changes). Strict reading also met ('removed from the scope'). V1 (304031): primary met (same rule 1: 'evaluated to determine if they should proceed', plus rule 3 on reassessing removed routes). Strict reading is arguable: rules 1a/1b say routes impacting lanes or parking 'will be removed', but the list itself only says it 'may be revisited', so linking the list to removal takes a step. COUNT: All three versions list the same 14 entries for re-evaluation and the same 13 for 'continue as planned'. Splitting the multi-segment entries (93 St + 84 Ave; 93 Ave/82 St/94 Ave + 75 St; Grovenor as three streets) gives 18. UNBUILT at Attachment 3's 2026-08-10 status date: all 14 are shown as not started. 84 Ave (79-83 St), 92A Ave/86 St/alley and 93 St/84 Ave are 'Tender awarded. Construction has not yet started'. Six routes are marked 'installation in 2026 is no longer viable' (not tendered). Five sit under 'Other: ... do not have a delivery plan and schedule'; I read 'no delivery plan' as not started, and 50 St (101-109A) is also described as 'paused for reconsideration'. Attachment 3 names one route '93 Street/84 Avenue (89 Street to 82 Avenue)', while Attachment 5 has '93 Street (82 Avenue to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 Street to 89 Street)'. I treated them as the same route. ALTERNATIVE STATUS DATE (2026-08-26): I found no separate dated City record. The City project page returned 502, so no route is shown to differ. CLASSIFICATION: V2 (primary): Partially supported, because the deferral element fails while count = 14 and all 14 are unbuilt. Original: Supported (Supported under the strict reading too). V1: Supported under the primary reading, and under the strict reading only if the list is linked to rules 1a/1b. The finding is VERSION-SENSITIVE and must say so beside the verdict. BUDGET: the report says approval 'would not result in any changes required to the existing capital profile CM-20-0330 ... or associated borrowing bylaws.'

claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2022-11-30 and 2026-09-25, Councillors Karen Principe and Jennifer Rice brought two motions at City Council that sought to leave about $50 million ($45M-$55M) in CM-20-0330, directed the released funds to named destinations, and Council defeated both.
claims.interpretation_notes: Two candidate motions were found, both jointly brought (Principe moved, Rice seconded, so both the primary and co-sponsorship readings of 'brought' are met), on separate occasions, and both defeated at City Council. MOTION A: Fall 2023 SCBA, Capital Budget Amendment 2 (re-stated), meeting of 2023-11-21 and continuations. Text: 'reduced by $50,000,000 ($16,350,000 in 2024, $16,825,000 in 2025, and $16,825,000 in 2026) with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt'. Result: Defeated 4 to 8. Base $100,000,000 (CBA 7, carried 2022; no later adjustment found). Remainder $50,000,000 (reviewer's calculation), which meets both the primary band and the at-least-half alternative. Destination: 'a funding reduction from tax-supported debt', which I read as a reduction in borrowing, so met. The postponed text named 'to go towards the tax levy' but was superseded by the re-statement that was put. MOTION B: Fall 2024 SCBA, Capital Budget Amendment 2, meeting of 2024-12-02 and continuations. Text: 'decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery'. Result: Defeated 4 to 7. Reduction $67,300,000 and remainder $32,700,000 on a $100M base (reviewer's calculation). That fails the primary band and meets the at-least-half alternative. Destination: arguable. 'With funding from tax-supported debt' names the funding line being reduced, which implies less borrowing, but it is weaker than Motion A's wording. CLASSIFICATION: Supported fails because only one motion meets the $45M-$55M band. Partially supported applies, since at least one jointly brought reduction motion was defeated. Under the alternative amount band, both motions qualify, giving Supported if Motion B's debt wording counts as a named destination and Partially supported if not. The finding is therefore definition-sensitive on the amount band and on the destination rule for Motion B. Under the co-sponsorship reading the classification is unchanged. Other recorded motions (qualification 4): 2023 CBA 3 (Rice moved, Principe seconded; '$26,808,000 be reduced from the 2024 capital budget', no profile named) was withdrawn. 2025-09-16 item 10.13: T. Cartmell moved, Principe seconded, 'That all current construction work cease immediately on bike lane projects ... pending a complete review', defeated 4 to 9 (Rice in favour). This is a pause motion, not a budget cut. Rice appears as a member in the 2022-2025 minutes, not in the 2026 attendance lists.

calculations_needed: Motion A (2023, reviewer's calculation): base $100,000,000 (2022 CBA 7). Reduction $16,350,000 + $16,825,000 + $16,825,000 = $50,000,000. Remainder $100,000,000 - $50,000,000 = $50,000,000. Within $45M-$55M: yes. Reduction 50%, so at least half: yes. Destination: reduction in tax-supported debt. Brought: primary yes, co-sponsorship yes. Defeated 4-8.

Motion B (2024, reviewer's calculation): base $100,000,000. Reduction $33,650,000 + $33,650,000 = $67,300,000. Remainder $32,700,000. Within $45M-$55M: no. 67.3% reduction, so at least half: yes. Destination: 'with funding from tax-supported debt' (arguable). Brought: primary yes, co-sponsorship yes. Defeated 4-7.
Base range at which Motion B would meet the primary band (reviewer's calculation): $67,300,000 + $45,000,000 = $112,300,000 up to $67,300,000 + $55,000,000 = $122,300,000.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A capital profile showing the approved total at December 2024 between $112.3M and $122.3M, with Motion B's wording read as naming a destination (to Supported).
A third jointly brought motion found in unsearched minutes that meets the primary band, names a destination and was defeated (to Supported).
Evidence that the minutes misrecord the mover, seconder or result of either motion.
claims.suggested_one_line: Principe and Rice twice moved to cut the bike-lane capital profile and lost both times. The 2023 motion would have left $50 million, but the 2024 motion would have left about $32.7 million.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Partially supported. Councillor Karen Principe moved and Councillor Jennifer Rice seconded two amendments at City Council budget meetings, and both were defeated. In November 2023 the amendment would have cut CM-20-0330 by $50 million 'with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt', leaving $50 million of the $100 million approved; it lost 4-8. In December 2024 the amendment would have removed all 2025 and 2026 funding ($67.3 million by our calculation), leaving about $32.7 million; it lost 4-7. So only one attempt matches 'cut it to $50M'. Under a looser 'cut by at least half' reading, both attempts qualify.
suggested_tldr: Two Principe/Rice amendments to cut CM-20-0330, in 2023 and 2024, were both defeated at City Council.
The 2023 amendment would have left $50M. The 2024 amendment would have left about $32.7M (our calculation).
The funding 'destination' in both was a reduction in tax-supported debt.
